review_note: At line 739 the source's Tor-independent (in particular flat g) cartesian base-change square makes the natural mate Rg'_*a' -> a Rg_* an isomorphism. The draft preserves the canonical arrow direction, Tor-independence and all qcqs hypotheses; it does not incorrectly claim the separate pullback duality comparison is always invertible.
statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{matrix}
\]
where $f$ and $g$ are *Tor-independent*, meaning the higher Tor sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ over $\mathcal O_Y$ vanish. Write $a=a_f$ and $a'=a_{f'}$ for the respective right adjoints of derived pushforward. The usual derived base-change map is $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$; under Tor-independence it is an isomorphism. Its adjoint mate is the isomorphism $\xi:Rg'_*a'\xrightarrow{\sim} a Rg_*$. The duality base-change map is the natural transformation $\alpha:L(g')^*a\to a' Lg^*$ obtained by composing unit $\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^*$, $\xi^{-1}$, and counit $L(g')^*Rg'_*\to\mathrm{id}$. Then the canonical adjoint-mate transformation $\xi:Rg'_*a'\to a\,Rg_*$, considered as a natural transformation from $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, is an isomorphism. This holds if $g$ is flat, and more generally whenever $f$ and $g$ are Tor-independent; the square need not be proper.
hypotheses: Cartesian qcqs square, g flat or f and g Tor independent, and right adjoints as defined.
conclusions: The canonical mate Rg'_*a'→a Rg_* is an isomorphism.

more generally that $f$ and $g$ are Tor independent. Then

review_note: At line 817 the pinned theorem has two if-and-only-if support criteria, first for D^+_QCoh inputs then for unbounded D_QCoh, and a third implication assuming a commutes with direct sums. The reconstruction precisely keeps both quantifier scopes, restriction comparison, closed support, and the direct-sum condition.
statement: Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. In the cartesian open square $U=X\times_YV\xrightarrow{j'}X$, $V\xrightarrow{j}Y$ with $V\subseteq Y$ quasi-compact open, write $f_V:U\to V$ and $a_V$ for the right adjoint of $R(f_V)_*$. The *restriction comparison* is $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_V(j^*K)$, obtained from the open-immersion case of the duality base-change transformation. A complex is *supported on* a closed subset if all its cohomology sheaves vanish outside that subset. Set $T=Y\setminus V$. Then: (1) $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ if and only if for every $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$, the object $a_f(Q)$ is supported on $X\setminus U$. (2) The same equivalence holds without the plus/bounded-below restrictions: $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism for all $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ iff $a_f$ takes every object supported on $T$ to one supported on $X\setminus U$. (3) If $a_f$ preserves arbitrary direct sums, then the equivalent conditions in (1) imply the equivalent conditions in (2).
hypotheses: f qcqs; V quasi-compact open, U inverse image, and a_f right adjoint; direct-sum preservation for part (3).
conclusions: Restriction comparison is characterized by preservation of cohomological support, with bounded and unbounded variants.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-when-sheafy}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes. Let $a$ be the right adjoint to
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
Let $V \subset Y$ be quasi-compact open with inverse image $U \subset X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $Q \in D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
supported on $Y \setminus V$ the image $a(Q)$ is supported on
$X \setminus U$ if and only if (\ref{equation-sheafy})
is an isomorphism on all $K$ in $D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
\item For every $Q \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
supported on $Y \setminus V$ the image $a(Q)$ is supported on
$X \setminus U$ if and only if (\ref{equation-sheafy})
is an isomorphism on all $K$ in $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
\item If $a$ commutes with direct sums, then the equivalent conditions of
(1) imply the equivalent conditions of (2).
\end{enumerate}

statement: Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. In the cartesian open square $U=X\times_YV\xrightarrow{j'}X$, $V\xrightarrow{j}Y$ with $V\subseteq Y$ quasi-compact open, write $f_V:U\to V$ and $a_V$ for the right adjoint of $R(f_V)_*$. The *restriction comparison* is $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_V(j^*K)$, obtained from the open-immersion case of the duality base-change transformation. A complex is *supported on* a closed subset if all its cohomology sheaves vanish outside that subset. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume either (a) $f$ is flat and of finite presentation, or (b) $Y$ is Noetherian. Then for *each* quasi-compact open $V\subseteq Y$ and $U=f^{-1}(V)$, the comparison $\rho_K:a_f(K)|_U\to a_{f|_U}(K|_V)$ is an isomorphism for all $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$. Equivalently, for bounded-below quasi-coherent-derived $Q$ supported on $Y\setminus V$, $a_f(Q)$ is supported on $X\setminus U$. This conclusion is stated for bounded-below inputs, not automatically for the entire unbounded category.
hypotheses: f proper qcqs with either flat finite presentation or Noetherian base.
conclusions: Right adjoint commutes with restriction to quasi-compact opens on D_QCoh^+, equivalently preserves closed supports.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-noetherian}
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism. If\footnote{This proof works for those
morphisms of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes such that
$Rf_*P$ is pseudo-coherent for all $P$ perfect on $X$. It follows
easily from a theorem of Kiehl \cite{Kiehl} that this holds if
$f$ is proper and pseudo-coherent. This is the correct generality
for this lemma and some of the other results in this chapter.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat and of finite presentation, or
\item $Y$ is Noetherian
\end{enumerate}
then the equivalent conditions of Lemma \ref{lemma-when-sheafy} part (1)
hold for all quasi-compact opens $V$ of $Y$.
